findings.reason: the plan names the wrong identifier and would send a node to a ref name incompatible with the existing namespace it is told to mirror.
findings.text: the deliverable pins under `refs/reckon/archive/<run-id>` "as it does for a dirty tree", but the dirty path assembles the ref as `ARCHIVE_REF_PREFIX + path.name` (reckon/crew/routing.py:2224), and `path.name` is the worktree directory name, which §7 says equals the node id, not the run id; the 13 existing refs under `refs/reckon/archive/` are 12 node-id-named and one run-id-named, so a node following the plan literally mints a second, run-id-named ref for a tree whose dirty sibling uses the node id, diverging from the path the phrase "as it does for a dirty tree" requires it to reuse

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_pinnable_unique_commits` (reckon/crew/routing.py:1591), the measurement gate (routing.py:804), the pin branch (routing.py:2206), the confinement refusal message (routing.py:2112-2116) and the cited run `r-20261008T122151393511-cfs-point-jet-custom-rule` all resolve; the run-id citation resolves to a live run directory.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §6 declares two negative controls, one per deliverable ("keeps pinning to dirty trees only" falsifies the pin-release bullet; "restores the refusal" falsifies the already-removed bullet), each auditable against the four done-when bullets.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the tests build temporary repositories and the two control logs are written under the run directory, which is durable GPFS, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name or ticket number is introduced by §6.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6 specifies the archive ref as `refs/reckon/archive/<run-id>`, but the dirty path it tells the worker to mirror builds that ref from the worktree directory name, so the identifier named is the wrong one.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the section's two done-when halves (pin a clean abandoned tree; tolerate an already-removed one) touch one function path on the same run class and close on one test file, so one verdict closes the node; the two prior findings on this section were answered by adding the second control rather than splitting, and nothing since has changed what it describes.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §6 names its sequencing dependency (`r-20261012T051827498181-a-worktree-release-is-whole`, merged as 2e44591a1, an ancestor of HEAD) and §7 names §6; no needed dependency is absent.
